name: Weno'iak the Enlightened

facts.text: Level 68, 30,000 health. Pulling him brings eight wi'voron cuirassiers and eight warsteeds. Casts Weno'iak's Lights (350 Spirit) and Weno'iak's Annihilate (450 Spirit, radius 500).

The drakoran of the city come in five clans whose names echo their lords': drau'gyn (Dra'argus), dry'ak (Dura'ek), syhr'phint (Sys'sro), vyr'em (Vera'erius) and wi'voron (Weno'iak); the lords' linked packs are of their own clan. The clan reading is inferred from names and packs.

story:
Weno'iak leads the wi'voron, the clan of reeves and advisors and of the drakoran cavalry, and he is the one the other lords call when they need to think. He took the scholars' observatory for his own and is said to read in the books the others burned. The Enlightened, they call him, and his light is no fire: it strikes at the spirit and breaks men from the inside. His cuirassiers and their warsteeds keep the yards of the colleges, and they ride when he rides.

The reeves. The wi'voron are the reeves and advisors of the drakoran host, occupiers and sicklemen and acaters who buy in the stores, and above all the cavalry: cuirassiers on warsteeds, the only drakoran who ride. Weno'iak is their lord, and the one the other lords call when they need to think. He took the readers' observatory and the colleges' stable-yards together, so that he could study by night and ride by day.

The light. He is said to read in the books the other lords burned; the readers of Caer Gothwaite suspect he saved some on purpose, and that he has been teaching himself from them. The Enlightened, his clan calls him, and his light is no fire: Weno'iak's Lights strike at the spirit and break men from inside, and his Annihilate does it to everyone around his target at once. His eight cuirassiers and their eight warsteeds keep the yards and ride when he rides. The Camelot loremasters think he is the most dangerous of the five, not because he is the strongest, but because he is the one who is learning.
legend:
Eight cuirassiers and eight warsteeds come with him, so that is seventeen pulls in one. Spread out against his Annihilate, which hits everyone near its target, and bring spirit resist. Off-tanks on the cavalry, and kill the warsteeds before their riders tire of walking.

The readers of Caer Gothwaite would pay a great deal for whatever books he has; Albion raiders have looked, and found only ash and a few torn pages in his observatory. The warsteeds die faster than their riders; kill them first and the cuirassiers walk. His Lights land on one target at a time, his Annihilate on everyone near it, so the casters spread wide.

loremasterTopic.text: The Enlightened. His clan rides warsteeds, and he burns men with a light that is not fire.

bookPage: The riders took the stable-yards of the colleges and our observatory with them, and their lord, my fishermen say, sits in the observatory at night with a lamp. One of them swears he saw books on the table: our books, the ones we thought had burned. If that is so, he saved them on purpose. I do not know whether to be grateful or afraid. The fishermen say his light is not fire, that it breaks men from inside, and that he has learned it somewhere. I fear I know where. We taught one pupil too well already. I would not have us teach another.
